interpretations: Count rows in constructorStandings per constructor (one row per race the constructor appears in), compare to the average rows per constructor computed only over constructors that have at least one standings record, and show the top 10 by (count − average).
Same count, but the average is computed over all constructors in the constructors table, including those with zero standings records (average = total standings rows ÷ number of constructors).
Same as interpretation 1, but "number of standings records" means distinct races (distinct raceId) per constructor rather than raw rows.
Same as interpretation 1, but "number of standings records" means distinct seasons (years, via races) in which the constructor has standings records.
"Furthest above the average" read as the largest signed difference (count − average), listing only constructors above the average.
"Furthest above the average" read as the largest absolute difference, which may include constructors below the average.
Difference shown as a raw number (count − average), possibly with decimals.
Difference shown rounded to a whole number or a fixed number of decimal places.
Difference shown as a percentage or ratio relative to the average rather than as a raw difference.
Ties in difference at the 10th place: return exactly 10 rows, with an arbitrary tie-break.
Ties in difference at the 10th place: include all tied constructors, possibly returning more than 10 rows.
Ties in difference at the 10th place: return exactly 10 rows, with a deterministic tie-break such as the constructor id.
Nationality is taken from constructors.nationality, joined on constructorId.
Output columns: constructorId, nationality, standings record count, difference from average; ordered by difference descending.
Output also includes the average itself as a column, alongside the four requested columns.
The average is taken across constructors within the same nationality, rather than across all constructors.
"Constructor standings records" read as constructorResults rows instead of constructorStandings rows.
Missing interpretations:
Average computed over constructors in the standings table, but the count and average are taken per season (average standings records per constructor per season) rather than overall.
Standings records limited to constructors with a non-null or valid position (rows where position or positionText is present), excluding unranked rows.
Difference shown as a ratio (count ÷ average) rather than a subtraction.
Average computed as the median per constructor rather than the mean.

Output includes all constructors (not only those above average) with the top 10 chosen purely by signed difference, where constructors lacking a nationality are still included (left join versus inner join).
queries:
SELECT constructorId, COUNT(*) AS cnt, COUNT(*) - (SELECT AVG(c) FROM (SELECT COUNT(*) AS c FROM constructorStandings GROUP BY constructorId)) AS diff
FROM constructorStandings
GROUP BY constructorId
ORDER BY diff DESC
LIMIT 10;
SELECT CAST((SELECT COUNT(*) FROM constructorStandings) AS REAL) / (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM constructors)
SELECT c.name, COUNT(DISTINCT cs.raceId) AS num_races
FROM constructorStandings cs
JOIN constructors c ON cs.constructorId = c.constructorId
GROUP BY c.constructorId, c.name;
SELECT c.name
FROM constructors c
JOIN constructorStandings cs ON c.constructorId = cs.constructorId
JOIN races r ON cs.raceId = r.raceId
GROUP BY c.constructorId
ORDER BY COUNT(DISTINCT r.year) DESC
LIMIT 1;
SELECT c.name
FROM constructors c
JOIN results r ON r.constructorId = c.constructorId
GROUP BY c.constructorId, c.name
HAVING COUNT(*) > (
  SELECT AVG(cnt) FROM (
    SELECT COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM results GROUP BY constructorId
  )
)
ORDER BY COUNT(*) - (
  SELECT AVG(cnt) FROM (
    SELECT COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM results GROUP BY constructorId
  )
) DESC;
WITH totals AS (
  SELECT c.constructorId, c.name, SUM(cr.points) AS total_points
  FROM constructorResults cr
  JOIN constructors c ON c.constructorId = cr.constructorId
  GROUP BY c.constructorId, c.name
)
SELECT name
FROM totals
ORDER BY ABS(total_points - (SELECT AVG(total_points) FROM totals)) DESC
LIMIT 1;
